title: What If You Flew to Mars and Back?

scenes.text: What if you flew to Mars and back? The trip itself is the dangerous part.
A round trip takes about 960 days: 180 out, 600 on the surface, and 180 home.
In deep space, radiation hits you at about 1.9 millisieverts a day, nearly three times the dose on Mars.
Even the Martian surface adds about 0.7 millisieverts a day, similar to the dose on the space station.
Add it all up and the round trip delivers about 1.1 sieverts of radiation, measured by NASA's Curiosity rover.
That's right at the one-sievert career limit space agencies use, and a big solar storm could push it higher.
